question.text: A Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund (Balanced Advantage Fund) is characterized by which of the following features?

answer.text: It maintains a fixed 50:50 allocation between equity and debt at all times
It must invest a minimum of 65% in equity at all times
It dynamically manages equity and debt allocation based on market conditions, with no fixed minimum or maximum for either asset class
It invests only in equity derivatives and debt instruments, not in direct equity

explanation.text: The Logic: A Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund (also known as a Balanced Advantage Fund) is an open-ended scheme that invests in equity and debt and manages that mix dynamically based on the fund manager's models and market conditions. The defining feature is the active, model-driven shift between equity and debt rather than a fixed allocation. The Trap: Unlike Aggressive Hybrid or Balanced Hybrid funds, the equity-debt split here is not anchored to a fixed band. The scheme is not restricted to derivatives alone; it can hold direct equity and debt instruments. Note: Anchor your answer to the source-supported description: open-ended dynamic asset allocation between equity and debt, managed dynamically. Treat any specific numeric range or tax-structuring claim as something that needs its own source.
